nodes.title: Ind-fppf ring maps
nodes.statement: A ring map R→B is ind-fppf if B is a filtered colimit, in commutative R-algebras, of faithfully flat finitely presented R-algebras. Equivalently every R-algebra map C→B with C finitely presented factors C→D→B with D faithfully flat and finitely presented over R. The indexing category is filtered and small in a fixed universe; a general faithfully flat map need not satisfy this predicate.
hypotheses: R→B is a map of ordinary commutative unital rings; filtered diagrams are small in the fixed universe.
proofSteps: Use the finite-presentation factorization criterion for filtered algebra colimits; include faithful flatness in every approximating stage.
Descend finite equations and maps to finite stages; source footnote 13 explains preservation under composition.
acceptance: R→R[X] is ind-fppf.
Z→Q is flat but fails ind-fppf.

nodes.title: The pro-fppf site
nodes.statement: A map X′→X is pro-ppf if, locally on source and target in affine charts, its ring map is a filtered colimit of flat finitely presented algebras. A single faithfully flat pro-ppf morphism is called pro-fppf. These covers are fpqc covers; no topology is generated by arbitrary faithfully flat maps alone.

Relate the resulting topology to the existing fppf and fpqc topologies.

nodes.title: The Bégueri smooth resolution
nodes.statement: For a commutative finite locally free group G over a scheme S, use its existing Cartier dual X=G* and define H=Res_(X/S)G_m and Q as the affine group of symmetric multiplicative two-cocycles on X. The coboundary map H→Q has kernel G and is an fppf epimorphism. Thus 0→G→H→Q→0 is a functorial short exact sequence of fppf sheaves, H and Q are smooth affine commutative S-groups, and H→Q is faithfully flat and finitely presented. Over affines, no new Cartier dual is defined.
hypotheses: S is a scheme; G is a commutative finite locally free S-group.
proofSteps: Represent H by finite-locally-free Weil restriction. Represent Q by the symmetry and cocycle equations inside the affine group of invertible functions on X×X.
Identify the kernel using Cartier duality. The vanishing of the local group-extension sheaf Ext¹(X,G_m), requested from SF.2, makes the coboundary locally surjective.
Use the explicit cocycle resolution to obtain smoothness of Q; do not replace it by a pointwise quotient.
acceptance: The sequence remains exact on animated fppf algebras after FC.3 constructs the site.
Formation is compatible with arbitrary base change.

For the reverse direction use the parent’s gerbe of trivializations and its tautological vector bundle.

On quasi-compact X the rank function has finite image and clopen fibres; equalize positive ranks by direct sums on these finite rank strata. Do not assert finitely many connected components.

nodes.title: Twisted bundles with an ample invertible sheaf
nodes.statement: Let X be quasi-compact and separated with an ample invertible sheaf, and let 𝒢→X be a G_m-gerbe with torsion class. Then 𝒢 has a finite locally free weight-one sheaf of constant positive rank. The construction reduces to finite type over Z and improves the codimension of the non-locally-free locus of a coherent twisted sheaf until that locus is empty.

proofSteps: Spread out the finite gerbe data and the ample bundle to a finite-type Z-model; affine Gabber supplies enough local twisted bundles.

For a class killed by n, select n+1 coherent twisted sheaves, finite locally free at prescribed complementary points and of common generic rank r. The sum of r^n copies of each and their tensor product both have weight one, since nα=0. On a G_m-gerbe tensor weights add as integers: transport weight n+1 back to weight one with a chosen invertible weight −n sheaf, or make the construction on a μ_n-gerbe lift.

Use Serre generation and the high codimension of the determinantal bad cone to choose a morphism with controlled kernels. de Jong Claim 3.22 obtains such a section after a finite flat Z-extension: the complement of the bad closure is an open of affine space, surjective over Z, so the imported incomplete-Skolem theorem applies with empty local conditions.
Push the kernel back along the finite faithfully flat extension; its nonfree locus improves in codimension. Iterate through the finite dimension of the model.

sourceIssues.printed: The nilpotent binomial argument claims that the tensor exponent itself annihilates the reduced K-class.
